subject: Culture
title: Hindu Temple Cosmology
description: A quick, practical guide to Hindu Temple Cosmology.

hook.text: Angkor Wat encodes the Hindu creation myth in stone. Its towers map Mount Meru, home of the gods.

buildup.text: Every Hindu temple is a microcosm. The sanctum represents the cave of the heart; the tower reaches heaven.

discovery.text: The 'garbhagriha'—womb chamber—is dark and small, forcing worshippers into intimate contact with the divine.

twist.text: Temple placement follows astronomical alignments. Konark's Sun Temple is oriented so sunrise hits the entrance.

climax.text: The temple doesn't represent the cosmos. In Hindu thought, it IS the cosmos made walkable.

punchline.text: Enter a temple and you walk through the universe.

quiz.question: What is the 'garbhagriha' in a Hindu temple?

details.summary: Hindu temples are not mere buildings — they are models of the cosmos in stone. The temple's layout maps the universe from outer chaos to inner divinity, guiding worshippers through a spatial journey from the profane threshold to the sacred garbhagriha (womb chamber) housing the deity.
details.whyItMatters: Hindu temple design demonstrates how architecture can encode an entire cosmology. Walking through a temple is walking through the structure of the universe from creation to the divine center.
takeaways: The garbhagriha (womb chamber) is the temple's innermost sacred room
Temple layout maps the journey from chaos to divine order
The shikhara (tower) represents Mount Meru — the cosmic mountain

faq.question: What is the garbhagriha?
faq.answer: The garbhagriha (literally 'womb chamber') is the temple's innermost sanctum, a small, dark room containing the main deity image. Only priests typically enter.

faq.question: How is a Hindu temple laid out?
faq.answer: A traditional Hindu temple follows vastu purusha mandala — a sacred geometric plan. The entrance faces east (toward the rising sun). Worshippers pass through the mandapa (pillared hall), progressively moving from light to darkness, from large to small spaces, toward the garbhagriha at the center.
